from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are arrows representing direction and magnitude.",
            "Dot product projects one vector onto another.",
            "The shadow length measures the projection magnitude.",
            "This reduces 2D interaction to 1D scalar.",
            "The dot product captures their geometric alignment."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Projection Intuition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        vec_v = Vector([1.5, 1.0], color="#FF5733")
        vec_w = Vector([2.0, 0], color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.place_at_grid(vec_v, "C2")
        self.play(Create(vec_v))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.place_at_grid(vec_w, "C4")
        self.play(Create(vec_w))
        
        proj_line = DashedLine(vec_v.get_end(), [vec_v.get_end()[0], 0, 0], color="#33FF57")
        self.add(proj_line)
        self.play(Create(proj_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))
        proj_point = Dot(point=[vec_v.get_end()[0], 0, 0], color="#3357FF")
        self.play(FadeIn(proj_point))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining Duality: The Linear Functional", [
            "A fixed vector defines a linear functional.",
            "It maps input vectors to scalar outputs.",
            "This machine acts as a weight filter."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        w_vec = Vector([1, 1], color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(v_vec, 'D2')
        self.play(Create(v_vec))
        label_v = Tex("v", color=BLUE).next_to(v_vec.get_end(), RIGHT)
        self.play(Write(label_v))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Dual Space", [
            "Visualize dot product results as level sets.",
            "These are parallel lines perpendicular to w.",
            "Vectors on the same line share dot products."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        w_vec = Vector([1, 1], color=YELLOW)
        
        # Grid setup
        lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(-3, 4):
            line = Line(start=[-3, -3 + i, 0], end=[3, 3 + i, 0], color=BLUE, stroke_width=2)
            lines.add(line)
        self.place_in_area(lines, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#F3FF33"))
        self.play(Create(lines))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#F3FF33"))
        self.place_at_grid(w_vec, "B2")
        self.play(GrowArrow(w_vec))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#F3FF33"))
        dot = Dot(color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, "D4")
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: The Power of Perspective", [
            "Duality bridges geometry and algebraic calculation.",
            "The dot product connects spatial properties.",
            "It turns geometric intuition into powerful algebra."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        eq_duality = MathTex(r"v \cdot w = |v||w|\cos(\theta)", color="#FFD700")
        mapping = MathTex(r"V \leftrightarrow V^*", color="#00FFFF")
        sum_total = MathTex(r"\text{Total Torque} = \vec{\tau} \cdot \vec{\omega}", color="#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.place_at_grid(eq_duality, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(eq_duality))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(mapping, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(mapping))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(sum_total, 'D3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(sum_total))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Dot Products and Duality: The Geometry of Interaction

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Projection Intuition
sections.content: Briefly define vectors as arrows. Introduce the dot product as the product of the length of one vector and the shadow (projection) cast by the other vector onto it. This transforms a 2D interaction into a 1D scalar value.
sections.example: Visualize a flashlight shining on a needle (vector v) resting on a table (vector w). The shadow length on the table represents the dot product.

sections.title: Defining Duality: The Linear Functional
sections.content: Explain that a dot product with a fixed vector 'w' is a machine that takes an input vector 'v' and outputs a scalar. This 'machine' is a linear functional. Duality states that every linear transformation from vectors to scalars is just a dot product in disguise.
sections.example: Think of 'w' as a 'filter' or 'gatekeeper'. If 'w' is a weight vector, the dot product calculates the 'total score' of a set of features (vector 'v').

sections.title: Visualizing the Dual Space
sections.content: Instead of arrows, represent the dot product result as a set of parallel lines (level sets). The vector 'w' defines the direction of the lines, and the dot product tells us which 'line' the input 'v' lands on.
sections.example: Use a topographic map: the vector 'w' points uphill, and the contour lines represent constant dot product values. Any vector 'v' landing on the same contour line has the same dot product with 'w'.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Power of Perspective
sections.content: Conclude by showing how duality allows us to bridge geometry (the vector) and algebra (the functional). Emphasize that the dot product is the bridge that turns geometry into calculation.
sections.example: A robotic arm (vector 'v') sensing a pressure field (defined by 'w'). The dot product calculates the total torque applied to the joint, showing how geometry informs physics.
